questions.question:
The following pie chart shows the number of workers of different categories A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H of a factory in 1995.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9370b5748af567e29777007848580b0687dfbf12fbaa3a5e7e94380577f6d8d4.png] 

If the number of workers in category B is increased by 10% and the number of workers in category D is decreased by 5% in 1996, then what is the total number of workers in categories B and D in 1996, if no. of workers in B was 1500 in the year 1995?
questions.solution:
**Concept Used:**

The concept of percentage is a number or ratio that can be expressed as a fraction of 100

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

⇒ In 1995, No. of workers is 1500

from the figure, the number of workers in category B is 15%

so, we can say

⇒ 15% = 1500

⇒ 1% = 100

In 1996, Category B increased by 10%

⇒ so, New population of Category B = Original Population x (100 + 10)/100 = 1500 x 110/100 = 15 x 110 = 1650

The number of workers in Category D is 25%

⇒ 1% = 100

⇒ 25% = 2500

In 1996, Category D decreased by 5%

⇒ so, New population of Category D = Original Population x (100 - 5)/100 = 2500 x 95/100 = 25 x 95 = 2375

⇒ Total population of the worker in Category B and Category D = New population of B + New population of D = 1650 + 2375 = 4025

⇒ **Hence, The total population of workers in Category B and Category D in 1996 is 4025.**

In a certain company, allocations to various sectors of the yearly budget per Rs. 7,200 crores are represented by this pie-diagram.

questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total budget = Rs. 7,200 crores

Angle for Infrastructure = 84.7°

**Formula used:**

Expenditure on Infrastructure = (Angle for Infrastructure / 360°) × Total Budget

**Calculation:**

Expenditure on Infrastructure = (84.7° / 360°) × 7,200 crores

⇒ Expenditure on Infrastructure ≈ 1,694 crores

**∴ The expenditure on Infrastructure is Rs. 1,694 crores.**

The pie chart 1 given below shows the runs scored by a player against 6 different countries during 2019-2020. Pie chart 2 shows the runs scored by the same player against the same 6 countries during 2020-2021. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2bc329c4ec52cfa380b059a3025f32124d3e828bfa6346fe8ac8c22a2d46d7a.png]

Find the difference between the total runs scored against New Zealand and Pakistan during 2019-2020 and the total runs scored against Sri Lanka and Pakistan during 2020-2021.
questions.solution:
**Solution:**

Runs scored against New Zealand during 2019-2020 = 14/100 × 4000 = 560 runs

Runs scored against Pakistan during 2019-2020 = 16/100 × 4000 = 640 runs

Total runs scored against New Zealand and Pakistan during 2019-2020 = 560 + 640 = 1200 runs

Runs scored against Sri Lanka during 2020-2021 = 20/100 × 5000 = 1000 runs

Runs scored against Pakistan during 2020-2021 = 15/100 × 5000 = 750 runs

Total runs scored against Sri Lanka and Pakistan during 2020-2021 = 1000 + 750 = 1750 runs

Required difference = 1750 - 1200 = 550 runs

**∴ Option 4 is the correct answer.**

questions.question:
The savings and expenditure of a family in a month on different heads is shown in the given pie chart. The family saves Rs. 8,000 per month.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00f3f219201565bd14cb5e3495818eb8a22e538ad302e0d506ec20b8ffc6daa1.png] 

Find the expenditure (in Rs.) on education.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Family saves Rs. 8,000 per month

Angle for Education expenditure = 30°

**Formula used:**

Expenditure for a category = (Angle for the category / 360) × Total monthly income

Total monthly income = Savings + Expenditure

**Calculation:**

First, find the total monthly income.

Angle for Savings = 60°

Total monthly income = Savings / (Angle for Savings / 360)

⇒ Total monthly income = 8,000 / (60 / 360)

⇒ Total monthly income = 8,000 / (1/6)

⇒ Total monthly income = 8,000 × 6

⇒ 48,000

Now, find the expenditure on Education.

Expenditure on Education = (30 / 360) × 48,000

⇒ Expenditure on Education = (1/12) × 48,000

⇒ Expenditure on Education = 4,000

**∴ The expenditure on education is Rs. 4,000.**

Find the total monthly expenditure (in Rs.) of the family.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total angle in pie chart = 360°

Angle for Savings = 60°

Monthly savings = Rs. 8,000

**Formula used:**

Total monthly income = (Monthly savings × 360°) / Angle for savings

**Calculations:**

Total monthly income = (8,000 × 360) / 60

⇒ Total monthly income = 48,000

Total expenditure = Total monthly income - Savings

⇒ Total expenditure = 48,000 - 8,000

⇒ Total expenditure = 40,000

**∴ The total monthly expenditure of the family is Rs. 40,000.**

questions.question:
The percentage distribution of the number of tires of different brands produced in a year by a certain factory is shown in the given pie chart. The total number of tires sold is 1350.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/22d7619f26bdacbc4b11dd50e782fd713b17a8ac033ae05f9c38ef1134a42c1b.png] 

What is the difference between the average number of Avon and Firestone tires sold together and the average number of Good year and Dunlop tires sold together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total number of tires sold = 1350

Percentage distribution of tires:

 
• Avon = 21%
 
• Firestone = 14%
 
• Goodyear = 12%
 
• Dunlop = 15%

**Concept and Formula used:**

Average = Total sum of items / Number of items

**Calculation:**

Number of Avon tires sold = 21% of 1350

⇒ Number of Avon tires sold = 0.21 × 1350 = 283.5

Number of Firestone tires sold = 14% of 1350

⇒ Number of Firestone tires sold = 0.14 × 1350 = 189

Number of Goodyear tires sold = 12% of 1350

⇒ Number of Goodyear tires sold = 0.12 × 1350 = 162

Number of Dunlop tires sold = 15% of 1350

⇒ Number of Dunlop tires sold = 0.15 × 1350 = 202.5

Average number of Avon and Firestone tires sold together:

⇒ (283.5 + 189)/2 = 472.5 / 2 = 236.25 

Average number of Goodyear and Dunlop tires sold together:

⇒ (162 + 202.5) / 2 = 364.5/ 2 = 182.25

Difference between the two averages:

⇒ 236.25 - 182.25 = 54

**∴ The difference between the average number of Avon and Firestone tires sold together and the average number of Goodyear and Dunlop tires sold together is 54.**
